name: CFGM - Coarse-to-Fine Grounded Memory for LLM Agent Planning
venue: EMNLP 2025 (Main Conference); Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, pp. 13029-13056, Suzhou, China, ACL. Also arXiv:2508.15305.
authors_affiliation: Wei Yang, Jinwei Xiao, Hongming Zhang (corresponding), Qingyang Zhang, Yanna Wang, Bo Xu (corresponding). All from the National Key Laboratory of Cognition and Decision Intelligence for Complex Systems, Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CASIA).
code_url: N/A (no official code repository linked in the paper, arXiv listing, or ACL Anthology page as of the survey date) [uncertain]
task_domain: LLM-agent planning / decision-making in interactive (text-based) environments: embodied household tasks (AlfWorld), web shopping (WebShop), and scientific reasoning (ScienceWorld).
problem_setting: Training-free, memory-augmented LLM agents for complex long-horizon interactive planning. Single-agent setting. CFGM uses an offline phase over a training task set (experience collection with trial-and-error reflection plus tips extraction) and an online inference phase over a held-out evaluation task set. No agent/model parameter training is performed; the LLM is enhanced purely via grounded memory injected as context. Four-fold cross-validation is used (train on one half, evaluate on the other half, and vice versa) so supervision is limited to the offline-collected trajectories generated by the agent itself, not human-labeled targets.
what_is_retrieved: Two types of memory: (1) the successful trajectory content of past task experiences (full successful trajectories), and (2) the experience-wise hybrid-grained 'tips' dictionary entries (high-level principles plus fine-grained scene-specific techniques) associated with the retrieved experiences. Both are grounded/distilled by the LLM from collected experiences.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes offline (experience pool B and tips dictionary TD are induced from the agent's own trial-and-error trajectories over training tasks). The store is frozen after the offline induction phase; it is not a static external corpus (docs/KB/APIs).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k similarity ranking (Faiss kNN top-k over task-description embeddings). The k is small and fixed (k=2 in main experiments); ablation shows k=2 or 3 is optimal and larger k (5) hurts due to conflicting tips. Objective is relevance-driven top-k retrieval of similar experiences, not minimal-set completeness recovery.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve (Faiss kNN of similar experiences) + Reuse (inject successful trajectories and tips as context) + Revise (online fine-grained key-information self-QA reflection corrects/adjusts plan on anomalies) + Retain (offline write of trajectories to experience pool and distilled tips to TD). All four phases are realized, though Retain is offline-only and Revise corrects the in-progress plan rather than the stored case. [uncertain on whether authors intend a formal 4-phase CBR claim]
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner; it frames its work as memory grounding / experience-based and feedback-based optimization for LLM agents. It realizes CBR-like mechanisms (retrieve similar experiences, reuse, revise via reflection, retain) under the 'grounded memory' framing.
retrieval_unit: Full successful trajectory (problem-solution experience) plus its associated hybrid-grained tips set (guideline-rules + fine-grained techniques). The retrievable key is the task description; the retrieved payload is the experience's successful trajectory and the corresponding tips dictionary entry TD[t_h].
index_source: Growing/episodic memory built offline (test-time-induced relative to deployment but offline relative to evaluation): the agent collects experiences via Reflexion-style trial-and-error over a training task set, guided by LLM-grounded coarse focus points; experiences are stored in pool B and distilled into a tips dictionary TD. The store is frozen for online evaluation (no online growth).
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index keyed by task description embedding (Faiss kNN), with experiences re-indexed by their associated task t_n; tips are organized as a dictionary keyed per-task (TD[t_n]). No graph or hierarchical topology.
retriever_type: Dense retrieval: kNN over textual embeddings using Faiss with the all-mpnet-base-v2 embedder (off-the-shelf sentence embedding).
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). The retriever uses a fixed pretrained text embedder (all-mpnet-base-v2) with Faiss kNN over task-description similarity; no contrastive/LM-feedback/RL training of the retriever is performed.
query_construction: Raw task description of the current evaluation task t_m is embedded and used as the query for top-k similar-experience retrieval (prior analysis based on task-description retrieval before inference).
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at the start of each evaluation task t=0): the top-k similar experiences and tips are retrieved once before the rollout begins and held fixed as context for the whole episode.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot for the experience/tips retrieval (done once per task before inference). Separately, online reflection is active/anomaly-triggered: when an abnormal observation is detected, the agent performs fine-grained key-information extraction and self-QA reflection (this is a reflection trigger, not an additional memory-retrieval call).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Experience/tips retrieval: fixed schedule (once per task at episode start). Online self-QA reflection: agent/environment-driven anomaly detection - real-time monitoring of observations o_{i+1}; a trigger fires on specific abnormal observations (e.g., 'Nothing happens', mismatch/error), after which key-information extraction (LLM_KIE) and key-information reflection (LLM_KIR) are invoked.
reranking: None. A single Faiss kNN top-k similarity stage is used with no reranking stage.
retrieved_context_refinement: Offline distillation rather than post-retrieval refinement: experiences are converted offline into hybrid-grained tips (compare success-vs-failure trajectories to extract error-avoidance tips, then refine success-specific tips). At retrieval time the successful trajectory content and tips are concatenated into context (ST and ET) without further reranking/compression. Online, key-information extraction structures the current trajectory but does not refine the retrieved memory.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill retrieval; memory items are trajectories and LLM-distilled tips, not tool docstrings).
index_content_separation: Partial: the index key is the lightweight task-description embedding while the heavy content (full successful trajectory + tips) is the payload loaded on retrieval. Tips are pre-distilled offline so a compact distilled artifact is stored alongside raw trajectories, but there is no explicit progressive-disclosure / index-then-content loading protocol. [uncertain]
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index or integration protocol; memory store is a static Faiss index after offline induction).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tool retrieval or inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation / case reuse: retrieved successful trajectories (ST) and experience tips (ET) are concatenated into the policy LLM's (LLM_CFGM) context to guide ReAct-style planning. On anomalies, retrieved successful trajectories also serve as context for the key-information self-QA reflection that produces a corrective plan (ref_i) injected back into the current trajectory.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan with per-step interleaved correction: top-k experiences and tips are retrieved once and prepended as exemplars/guidelines for the whole ReAct rollout; within the rollout, anomaly-triggered fine-grained key-information self-QA reflection produces in-line plan corrections appended to the trajectory step. No tree search / MCTS.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call/per-step within a rollout for the reflection correction (triggered at the step where an abnormal observation occurs); experience+tips context is per-answer (once at episode start). Underlying policy is ReAct (per think-act step).
adaptation_mechanism: Execution-feedback-driven revision via self-QA: retrieved successful cases/tips are reused largely verbatim as ICL exemplars/guidelines; when execution feedback signals an anomaly, the LLM grounds the current state into fine-grained key information (LLM_KIE) and performs self-reflective question-answer (LLM_KIR) over the current trajectory, key information, and similar successful trajectories to derive a corrective plan ref_i.
retrieved_item_representation: Mixed surface forms injected as text: (1) raw successful trajectory content (ST) and (2) distilled hybrid-grained tips (ET) which are free-text high-level principles plus fine-grained scene-specific techniques (structured note-like guidelines). Online corrections are free-text reflection/plan adjustments.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Hybrid: raw successful trajectory (low abstraction) combined with distilled hybrid-grained tips spanning high-level coarse principles (cross-task strategy/insight) and fine-grained scene-specific techniques (hint/rule). Coarse focus points additionally guide collection offline.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Relevance/self-reflection-based: (a) restricting retrieval to a small focused top-k (k=2/3) to avoid conflicting tips (ablation shows k=5 degrades performance), (b) hybrid-grained tips distilled by comparing success vs failure trajectories to encode error-avoidance, and (c) online fine-grained key-information self-QA reflection that detects environmental anomalies and corrects derailed plans. No retriever-aware training or distractor-aware SFT (training-free).
memory_type: Episodic experience pool (successful/failed trajectories) plus a distilled tips dictionary (guideline/insight memory). Combination of episodic memory and a workflow/guideline-style distilled memory; no skill-library program store or graph memory.
write_back: True (offline only). The agent stores collected trajectories (successful and failed) into the experience pool B during offline collection, and writes LLM-distilled hybrid-grained tips into the tips dictionary TD. No write-back occurs during online evaluation.
online_growth: No. The experience pool and tips dictionary are induced offline over the training tasks and frozen for online evaluation; the store does not grow at test/deployment time. Online reflection corrections are appended to the current trajectory only, not persisted to memory.
write_back_trigger: Offline, on-success-and-failure: during experience collection both successful and failed trajectories of a (eventually) solved task are stored in B; tips are then written reflectively after offline self-critique comparing success vs failure trajectories (and from single-success trajectories). No online/human-validated write-back.
failure_experience_usage: Success+failure contrastive (offline): failed trajectories paired with successful ones (C_compare) are fed to LLM_Tips to extract error-prevention tips; success-only trajectories (C_success) yield success-specific tips. At online retrieval, only successful trajectory content (tau_h^success) plus the distilled tips are injected as context (failures are used to derive tips, not surfaced directly).
memory_evolution_update: Append-only with offline refinement: trajectories are appended to the pool; tips per task are generated then expanded/refined (compare-trajectory tips, then success-specific tips appended). No online mutation, dedup-merge, forgetting, or link-and-evolve of stored entries after the offline phase.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval is fixed similarity top-k (Faiss kNN over off-the-shelf embeddings); it is not an RL/learned case-selection policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: AlfWorld (134 solvable tasks across 6 task types), WebShop (100 tasks; success rate and mean reward), ScienceWorld (100 tasks sampled from test set across diverse task types, up to 80 env steps). WebArena-Shopping (90/98 tasks) used in the out-of-distribution transfer ablation; WebArena referenced for ablation.
benchmark_family: embodied (AlfWorld), web (WebShop; WebArena-Shopping for OOD transfer), science/embodied-text (ScienceWorld).
baselines: ReAct, ExpeL, AutoGuide, QuBE, and ExpeL + QuBE (combination baseline). For the OOD transfer ablation: ReAct, ExpeL, AutoGuide. For the reflection ablation: template-free Self-QA Reflection and QA Reflection with fixed-question template (QuBE-style).
key_metrics: Success Rate (SR) as the primary metric across all environments; WebShop additionally reports mean Reward (attribute/option matching quality). Efficiency reported via offline tokens, online tokens-per-step, and average interaction turns.
headline_result: On AlfWorld CFGM reaches 91.00% +/- 0.82% SR vs ReAct 80.60% (+10.40 pts) and best memory baseline ExpeL+QuBE 85.07%. Also WebShop 85.0 +/- 1.3 mean reward and 57% SR, ScienceWorld 74% SR; CFGM consistently outperforms all baselines (using GPT-4-Turbo as policy model, GPT-4o as knowledge-extraction model).
ablations: (1) Component ablation on AlfWorld: ReAct 80.60 -> +FP 85.82 -> +ET 86.57 -> +KIR 85.82 -> ET+KIR 88.06 -> FP+ET+KIR (full CFGM) 91.00; removing FP drops SR to 88.06, showing FP improves collected-memory quality. (2) Top-k experience retrieval scope on tips quality (ReAct+ET): k=0 80.60%, k=1 82.09%, k=2 86.57%, k=3 86.57%, k=5 81.34% (peak at k=2/3). (3) OOD transfer WebShop->WebArena-Shopping: CFGM 25.1% SR vs AutoGuide 20.4%, ExpeL 18.5%, ReAct 10.2%. (4) Online reflection comparison on AlfWorld: Key Information Reflection 85.82% vs Self-QA Reflection 84.33% vs fixed-question QA Reflection 84.33%. (5) Generalizability across models (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to GPT-4.1) - CFGM beats ReAct and ExpeL across all. (6) Efficiency: CFGM has lowest online tokens/step (4681.4) and fewest online turns (14.32) among memory baselines.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (SR, reward) and efficiency are reported; no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are reported separately. The top-k ablation reports downstream SR vs k, not retrieval quality directly.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-based (SR, reward). Some process-adjacent signals: efficiency in interaction turns and tokens-per-step, and qualitative trajectory examples showing error recovery; no quantitative step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or retrieval-accuracy metrics.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported on AlfWorld. Offline tokens per training sample: CFGM 4068.5 (comparable to ExpeL 3888.2, more efficient than AutoGuide 4873.4). Online tokens-per-step: CFGM 4681.4 (lowest among memory baselines: ExpeL 5125.5, AutoGuide 4809.4, QuBE 4752.3; ReAct 1734.6 with no memory). Online interaction turns: CFGM 14.32 (fewest; ReAct 19.01, ExpeL 17.32, AutoGuide 16.55, QuBE 17.21), implying lower latency/cost.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k retrieval: Experience Retrieval Scope = 2 and Top-k Experience's Tips Selection = 2 (Faiss kNN). Max tips from compare trajectories = 5, max tips from success trajectory = 3. Max reflection retries (offline collection) = 3. Per-environment max env steps: AlfWorld 20, WebShop 15, ScienceWorld 80, WebArena-Shopping 20. No explicit token-budget cap or reranked-then-truncated selection beyond the fixed k. SR is binary task completion; WebShop reward is the attribute/option matching score (Eq.1-2).
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks; AlfWorld 134 tasks/6 types, WebShop 100 tasks from a 1.18M-product/12,087-instruction catalog, ScienceWorld 100 tasks across 30 task types/10 topics, WebArena-Shopping ~90 tasks). Not a new benchmark contribution.
builds_on: ReAct (reasoning-acting interleaving, used as the underlying policy), Reflexion (trial-and-error self-reflection used in offline experience collection), ExpeL (experience recall + insight extraction), AutoGuide (context-aware guideline extraction), QuBE (question-based belief-state reflection). Uses Faiss for retrieval and all-mpnet-base-v2 as the embedder.
contrasts_with: Single-granularity memory methods: ExpeL (holistic insight extraction), AutoGuide (scenario-specific guidelines), QuBE (fixed human-curated question templates for reflection), and the ExpeL+QuBE combination. CFGM argues these use single-granularity memory and fixed-question reflection; CFGM instead grounds coarse-to-fine (focus points, hybrid-grained tips) memory and uses flexible fine-grained self-QA reflection.
lineage: Experience/memory-augmented LLM-agent planning lineage (experience-based and feedback-based optimization for agents); sub-topic of growing-memory experience/case planners (Group C: RAG planning / experience-grounded agent memory). Successor in the ReAct -> Reflexion -> ExpeL/AutoGuide/QuBE line, adding LLM-grounded coarse-to-fine multi-granularity memory.
